Vampiric Draining

A Wraith (Stargate) draining a human's life force.

Power/Ability to:

Drain anything from people or objects.

The power to drain anything from an object, creature, or surroundings. Sub-power of Absorption and Vampiric Force Manipulation. Variation of Dependency. Not to be confused with Blood Absorption/Consumption.

Also Called[]

  • Vampiric Drain/Devouring/Feeding/Leeching/Siphoning

Capabilities[]

Users can drain anything (energy, souls, blood, etc.) from individuals, objects, or even their surroundings.

Applications[]

  • Absorbing Regeneration: The user drains to speed up their healing process.
  • Age Acceleration: The victim may rapidly age as a result of the draining.
  • Death Inducement: In the most extreme cases, the victim does not survive.
  • Enervation Inducement: The victims are generally exhausted after the draining, either temporarily or chronically.
  • Life Reduction: The victim's lifespan may be shortened.
  • Metabolization: The user drains for sustenance.
  • Self-Power Augmentation: The user's powers often increase after feeding.

Techniques[]

  • Bodily Fluid/Blood Consumption: Feed through absorption by ingesting the bodily fluids of others for sustenance, offensive, defensive, or regenerative purposes. Also having the ability, through Power Via Blood, to take power from others.
  • Blood Memory: Can access memories of those whose blood is consumed.

Variations[]

  • Draining Field Projection
  • Energy Vampirism
  • Emotional Vampirism
  • Memory Vampirism
  • Neuronal Vampirism
  • Life-Force Absorption
  • Element Drain
  • Energy Drain
    • Total Drain
  • Health Drain
  • Psychic Vampirism
    • Psionic Drain

Associations[]

  • Absorption
  • Dependency
  • Parasite Physiology
  • Vampire Physiology
  • Vampiric Force Manipulation

Limitations[]

  • May be limited to draining certain objects or from certain things, such as living people.
  • May be limited to draining certain materials, such as blood, life force, or souls.
  • May have a limit to how much can be drained.
    • Can take/be given too much.

Gallery[]

Luminous Valentine (That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime) can drain her victim's energy through contact and also convert that energy into pain.
Serpent Vampire (The Haunted House/Shinbi Apartment)
Victims of Wraith feeding (Stargate) rapidly age during the process...
...and are ultimately reduced to withered husks.
Using Midnight Bliss, Demitri Maximoff (Darkstalkers) drains a victim of blood.
Using Bio-Leech, Cole MacGrath (Infamous) drains bioelectric energy directly from people.
Because of its damaged DNA, Carnage (Ultimate Marvel) can use its tentacles to drain a target's bodily fluids, to the point of physical death.
Metroids (Metroid series) survive by draining other beings of their life energy.
After awakening her Metroid DNA, Samus Aran (Metroid) gained the power to drain energy from living beings and machines by physical contact.
With just a touch, Ann Marie LeBeau/Rogue (Marvel Comics) can drain anyone of their life force, abilities, memories, personality, and physical characteristics.
After being blown up by a nuclear missile, Superman (The Dark Knight Returns/DC Comics) drains a field of plants to heal.
Michael Morningstar (Ben 10) draining numerous DNAliens en masse.
As the Siphon, Severin (Buffy the Vampire Slayer Season Nine) can drain mystical energy from magic users, demons, vampires, and Slayers, either depowering them or killing them outright.
Imhotep (The Mummy) regenerates himself by draining others of their organs and fluids, mummifying them.
Keizer Ghidorah (Godzilla: Final Wars) draining Godzilla's energy with a bite.
Tetra (The Legend of Zelda: Phantom Hourglass) has been drained of her life force by Bellum, petrifying her.
Kain (Legacy of Kain series) draining a victim of blood from a distance.
DIO Brando (JoJo's Bizarre Adventure) draining a victim completely of his blood.
Osmosians like Aggregor (Ben 10) can drain other beings of life force and powers through physical contact.
Android 19 (Dragon Ball Z) draining Goku's ki.
Cell (Dragon Ball Z) draining a human's life force on a cellular level.
Moro (Dragon Ball Super) can drain life force to from anything to sustain himself, ranging from individuals to entire planets.
Fūka (Naruto) draining Naruto's chakra.
Angel (Buffy the Vampire Slayer) draining Buffy's blood.
Myotismon (Digimon Adventure) can drain either data from Digimon or blood from humans.
Evangeline A.K. McDowell (Negima) draining Negi's blood.
Moka Akashiya (Rosario + Vampire) draining Tsukune's blood.
Robin (Fire Emblem/Super Smash Bros.) uses Nosferatu to drain life energy from a target and feed it to himself.
As a dhampir, Rayne (BloodRayne) can drain blood from others to heal and sustain herself.
As his cyborg body lacks self-repair/fuel supply capabilities, Raiden (Metal Gear) can use Zandatsu to extract and drain an opponent's power cell to heal and recharge.
Vladats (Ben 10 series) can drain life force from anything, including Celestialsapiens, through their bite.
Whampire (Ben 10 series) struggling with the Vladat's urge to feed.
Jack of Blades (Fable) using the Drain Life spell.
Cybersix (Cybersix) lives by feeding of other Cybers akin to a vampire.
Buzzwole (Pokémon) draining Snorlax.
